findings.title: Cleanup service ticker interval reduced from 10 minutes to 1 minute
findings.body: In `CleanUpService.Run`, the ticker interval was changed from `time.Minute * 10` to `time.Minute * 1`, while the cleanup job timeout in `clean` remains `9 * time.Minute` (line 89). Running all background cleanup jobs (temporary files, snapshots, dashboard versions, images, annotations, invites, short URLs, and query history) every minute instead of every 10 minutes looks like leftover local testing code and will significantly increase background database and filesystem load.

findings.title: Debug logging left at Error level in annotation cleanup
findings.body: `CleanAnnotations` (lines 534, 537, 554, 557) and `CleanOrphanedAnnotationTags` (lines 576, 579) call `r.log.Error(...)` on every batch iteration even when no error occurred, and include the full slice of `ids` (up to `AnnotationCleanupJobBatchSize`) in the log fields. Because the cleanup job runs periodically and executes at least one batch per annotation type and tag check, this will spam error logs with large ID arrays during normal operation.

findings.title: Quadratic string concatenation when building SQLite DELETE query for large batches
findings.body: In `deleteByIDs`, when running on SQLite with `AnnotationCleanupJobBatchSize > 999`, the `IN` list is constructed in a loop using `values = fmt.Sprintf("%s, %d", values, v)` (lines 609-612). Because Go strings are immutable, this copies the growing `values` string on every element, resulting in O(N^2) allocations and CPU time in the batch size (e.g. ~32k iterations in the new test case). Use a `strings.Builder` or chunk the `DELETE` into batches of at most 999 parameters.

findings.title: Unbounded SQL parameter count in deleteByIDs can exceed PostgreSQL and MySQL limits
findings.body: `deleteByIDs` only guards against SQLite's parameter limit (line 608) and otherwise builds `DELETE FROM <table> WHERE id IN (?, ?, ...)` with `len(ids)` bound parameters. PostgreSQL and MySQL both enforce a maximum of 65,535 prepared-statement parameters (and older SQLite versions default to 999 when `len(ids) > 999`). If `annotation_cleanup_job_batch_size` is configured above 65,535, cleanup will fail with a database driver error on every run.
